content_sections.body_text: Use the present simple for a routine or a fact: ‘I run home after class. I live near the park.’ For practice, use a made-up address instead of private information. Read each line, cover it, and say it again with your own safe place or routine.
content_sections.title: Review routines and safe details

content_sections.body_text: Tap once for run and home, twice for af-ter, and twice for ad-dress. Say each part slowly, then join the parts without a new sound. Record one slow version and one normal version. Both versions must keep the same number of taps.
content_sections.title: Rehearse syllable boundaries

content_sections.body_text: Mai: ‘Please help me write my address on this form.’ An: ‘Yes. Tell me the address.’ Mai: ‘12 Park Road.’ An: ‘I’ll write it here.’ An is the writer, so the reply matches Mai’s request. Practise with a made-up address, then change the road name.
content_sections.title: Ask someone to write

content_sections.body_text: Give two safe facts and one routine with run. Then ask another person to write one fact. Speak both roles and write the lines from memory. Check: the ideas are facts or routines, run means fast movement on foot, the helper clearly does the writing, and the syllable count stays the same at normal speed.
content_sections.title: Say, write, and check
